rules.quote: Only use them in informal content.
rules.specification: Do not use exclamation marks in formal content like reports or briefings, unless quoting directly or presenting the character as literal input.

when: Except when quoting directly or presenting characters as themselves in technical instructions

rules.quote: Use them sparingly in less formal content such as promotional material and social media posts.
rules.specification: Do not use exclamation marks in urgent alerts, emergency warnings, or content where they create panic or stress.
rules.violation_condition: an exclamation mark used in emergency, warning, or stress-inducing content, creating a sense of panic or stress
when: In less formal content such as promotional material and social media posts
rules.why: E-1, G-2: Combines the rule on informal/sparing use with its specific prohibition on panic-inducing contexts tested by the 'Like this' / 'Not this' pair.

covers.quote: Write one exclamation mark: don’t overuse them
Don’t use exclamation marks too often.
Some people use multiple exclamation marks in social media. This is not suitable for government content.

rules.quote: At the end of each sentence you want to emphasise, use only one exclamation mark.
rules.specification: Never use more than one exclamation mark consecutively at the end of a sentence.
rules.why: G-1, G-4: The heading and surrounding paragraphs restate the rule to use only a single exclamation mark.
